A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CreatiDesign and provide readable text, equations, figures and tables that can be matched reliably. All 15 pages of v1 and 14 pages of v3 were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, a user study, generated design and editing examples, and component ablations in Tables 1–2 and Figures 5–8.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark results, user study, editing demonstrations and component ablations. Results retained from v1 still constitute original empirical results.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same encoders, LoRA adaptation, multimodal attention and masks. However, Figure 3 changes from a clean image followed by encoding and an explicit '+Noise' step to a noisy image entering the encoder. The text does not establish whether this is merely a schematic revision or a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic graphic-design dataset and curated benchmark, covering the same design categories and condition types. The movie-poster sequential-editing demonstration is also retained; no additional task or domain is evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same twelve comparators, and Figures 2 and 5–7 retain their corresponding comparison methods. GPT-4o remains in the qualitative comparisons. Citation removals do not remove evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The stated protocols remain unchanged: 400K training samples, 1,000 validation samples, the same evaluation metrics, and rank-256 FLUX.1-dev LoRA training for 100,000 steps with batch size 8. Both user studies report 50 evaluation reports on 30 samples using 1–10 ratings.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same layout-encoder, layout-attention-mask and subject-attention-mask ablations in Table 2 and Figure 8, plus the same sequential-editing case study. No robustness, sensitivity or error analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both present the same point estimates and user-study summaries. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, random-seed information, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the experimental figures retain the same numerical and qualitative results. For example, Table 1 reports average scores of 69.28 for CreatiDesign and 47.50 for FLUX.1-dev in both versions; Table 2 retains 12.13 sentence accuracy without the layout encoder.

T1.justification: The problem definition, semantic-layout formulation in Equation 1 and multimodal-attention formulation in Equation 2 are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: unified multi-condition generation, spatial attention masks, automated construction of a 400K-sample dataset, and improved adherence to user intent. The introductory condensation does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning semantic leakage, spatial binding, component contributions and editing consistency are retained. Both versions identify facial-detail preservation and dense-text generation as limitations associated with insufficient dataset coverage.

D1.justification: v3 removes the project-page link supplied on v1's title page. It also replaces the Gemini reference's model-specific URL with a malformed double-scheme URL. The implementation details, hardware, training duration and hyperparameters remain unchanged; actual resource availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Citation coverage is substantially reduced across subject-driven generation, layout control and graphic design, removing works including DreamO, COLE and LayoutDM. EasyControl and EliGen also disappear from methodological attribution, while Showmaker is added. The broad positioning remains similar, but the literature coverage changes substantially beyond citation-style conversion.

P1.justification: v3 condenses portions of the introduction, changes to author–year citations, updates authors and affiliations, and adds an acknowledgments section. Most prose and the scientific section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The conference template changes headings, headers, spacing and float placement. Figure 3 revises the noise depiction and schematic presentation. All eight figures and both tables are retained, with no new experimental displays.

improvement.justification: The experimental evidence and core conclusions remain unchanged. Modest prose and layout refinements are outweighed by removal of the project-page link, the malformed Gemini reference URL, and loss of explicit methodological attribution to EasyControl and EliGen. These create a limited decline in documentation and traceability without weakening the retained empirical evidence.
